title: Sweet and Sour Chicken or Turkey

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet and sour chicken or turkey is a dish made from tender poultry meat that is stir‑fried and coated in a sauce of vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and spices. It balances sweet and tangy flavors, creating a bright, aromatic taste popular in Asian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in China, where sweet‑sour combinations symbolize harmony.
Traditional sauce often includes pineapple, which enhances sweetness and adds a fruity aroma.
The sauce can be made with tomato ketchup or without it, using only vinegar and sugar.
It cooks quickly: the meat is fried first, then the sauce is added at the end to keep the chicken or turkey juicy.
Variations add vegetables such as bell pepper, carrot, and onion for extra texture and flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat (when using breast meat)
items.content: Poultry breast contains little saturated fat, making the dish suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is rich in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants in the sauce
items.content: Ingredients like ginger and garlic have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from pineapple (if used) boosts immune defense.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The sweet‑sour sauce can be high in sugar, which is not advisable for diabetes or weight control.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds significant sodium, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: People allergic to soy should use alternative sauces.

items.title: Cooking temperature
items.content: Overcooking the meat can create harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, typically with rice, noodles or vegetable sides. Garnish with fresh pineapple, green onions or sesame seeds for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in a pan or microwave, adding a splash of water to prevent the sauce from drying out.
